Alternative Lifestyles

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Life beyond the walls of societies norms and expectation, three people choose a path that works for them and the people they love

Summary:
This story is a little Wild Wild country and a little eat pray love.
Three people leave everything they have to to choose a new way of living; they reject all societies norms and expectations and create their own path. Forgoing their capital existence's to follow an alternative lifestyle, one that is centred around personal happiness for them and the people they love.


Further information:
Character 1
Mary used to be an ER doctor, she was married to big time doctor and had the ‘perfect’ life, but she got divorced, her life fell apart and she needed a change. She started by doing a 10 day Vipassana silent retreat at the Vipassana Centre near Cape Town. All their courses are completely free. Everything at the center is based on donations from “old students” people that have done multiple courses and have a regular practice. Mary eventually landed up being invited to live permanently at the center.

Vipassana is a non religious mindfulness way of living, it is the oldest form of Indian meditation. Modern day Vipassana practices are guided by one teacher MR Goenka: "Rather than converting people from one organised religion to another organised religion," said Mr. Goenka, "we should try to convert people from misery to happiness, from bondage to liberation and from cruelty to compassion."

The centre is in the middle of nowhere. As a permanent resident Mary takes care of the kitchen. A daily routine starts with a video talk from the guru and a meditation in the morning then there are three group meals a day, all vegan. During the course no one can talk to each other and no-one is allowed digital devices and the dress code is respectful by covering body parts. During the course and in general followers of Vipasssana practice, no violence, no illicit substance, not thinking or speaking ill of anyone and no sex.

Mary’s children are grown up and come visit her at the center. She has never been happier, she is glowing from the inside

Character 2
Boggon has ten children and him and his wife have been married for 38 years, the whole family lives and work on the Rose family estate. It started with food, a mission to create food that provides energy. Boggon spent years researching how the foods people eat today are infact robbing us of energy instead of giving us energy. It then became a way of life, a family business and a spiritual quest. Boggons theories on food and the food they produce are based on biblical studies, he has looked at what god and his closest ate and gone back in time and studies early man in order to farm and create foods that sustain life, instead of deplete it. Spiritually Boggons believes that all you have to do is be kind and believe in god and the rest will happen. If you do badly to others it will come back ten fold.

He has some crazy theories about how humans are being brain washed by Low-level frequencies being sent from an mine. Our water is poisoned as part of this brainwashing too. And that there are evil forces operating on very high frequencies keeping the world in chaos.

The rose family have created a heaven for themselves in world that no longer made sense to them. They are now getting to the point where they want to share their way of life with a broader community and create a village

This is what grandpa Rose, Boggons, says about their way of life: In a world full of toxins, chemicals, poisonous foods, opposition and plenty of negativity! Our purpose is to provide all the knowledge we have accumulated, so that you too, can be FREE!!!
Nobody in our family goes to doctors, are on any prescriptions or suffer from any sort of illnesses and we want you to experience that!!!
Food is medicine!

Character 3
A family that quit everything and are living on the road with their children. Home schooling them and seeing the world, while working remotely.

Press Release:


Choosing an Alternative Lifestyle
Would you reject a high-powered job and earning all the money you possibly could, while living in your dream home, in order to follow your inner truth? After years of passing each other like ships in the night, one family opted to reject the confines of society’s expectations by leaving the rat race, packing everyone into a camper van and living life on the open road.
Producer: Tarryn Crossman
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Watch the trailer


Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:05 Brian Wagner We come across various cross roads in our lives where we have to make various changes in our lives and whether you are on a spiritual path or on a commercial path. All humans our biggest thing that holds us back is the word fear.
2 00:121 Video vlog of the Cindy Alfrino Cindy: We have packed our room and we’ve packed the car full to bursting,
3 00:29 Cindy and Seth interview Cindy: It’s really difficult to choose something different because people dint understands it. But if that is what is going to bring you joy

Seth: you just got to do it, it will all work out in the end.
4 00:40 Alfreeno vlog Cindy: so, we are starting our adventure woohooo
5 00:44 Macfarlane link As we start the new year we set goals and plan for the successes of 2019 but what does success mean to you? Is it about owning your own home, paying off your car or having a really nice paying job? Well the people that you are about to meet have a different idea about success. And even though society may side eye them they are choosing to live life their own way.
6 01:07 Voice over and link to camera To society Brian Wagner was a picture of success. He had his own businesses, he was making lots of money and he had all the toys to prove it but 18 years ago he decided to quit his real-world life and follow his heart becoming a Vipassana Meditation teacher.
7 01:23 Brian Wagner interview My life 18 years ago was the yuppie life, I had the right house, drove the right car, I went to the right places on holiday, did all the right things that I believed society wanted me to be. I got to a stage where I had done a Vipassana meditation course, I found that what I had found for myself and what I had felt about myself was just totally different from who I really was. And after that I started making a conscious effort and change to what I do now.

Vipassana meditation is finding the stillness within yourself. Because through the gift of stillness you start understanding yourself.
8 02:15 Voice over More and more South Africans are struggling with the confines of society and opting for alternative life
9 02:22 Macfarlane In 2018 Cindy Alfino and her husband decided it was enough with the rat race, they packed up their 3 kids got into a revamp van and decided to explore southern Africa
10 02:32 Cindy and Seth Cindy: We took a really old camper van it’s from 1974

Seth: Over the months we stripped it and redid the inside

Cindy: Completely did the inside

Seth: we remodelled it to fit for a family of 5.
11 02:48 Alfino Vlog
12 02:52 Cindy and Seth interview Cindy: We left on the 1st of July 2018. First month in the van we were like what have we done? But this is amazing but Oh my Gosh, there’s 7,5 square meters of space
13 03:07 Cindy phone footage Cindy: We are making a make shift tray because we don’t have one so we got a tin one, tin foil one
Seth: To melt the cheese on
14 03:16 Cindy and Seth interview Cindy: We planned our first month so we knew we wanted to hit the East Coast up to Coffee bay we were on the coast
15 03:26 Cindy phone footage Cindy: This coastline man it is just all kinds of magic
16 03:32 Cindy interview Cindy: Then we went to Lesotho and did the whole of Lesotho and came down and did Durban up to St. Lucia and then headed inland up to Swaziland
17 03:44 Cell phone footage Seth: yeah
18 03:46 Seth and Cindy interview Seth: Life before the road was pretty standard I think. Typical family life – Cindy is an insurance broker and I’m an architect and kids all three of them went to school
Cindy: We were always just passing each other
Seth: And I felt I was missing time with the kids but also the kids would get presents and they didn’t really care about it and the kinds the rooms would get packed with presents and toys
Cindy: Constant
Seth: and I just like I didn’t want to bring them up like this they had to enjoy the finer things with just less and yeah it kind of made sense giving the kids a year of our lives where we just a family enjoying places and experiences and teaching them to live with less getting in touch with nature

19 04:30 Voice over Even though they are living on the road, Cindy still runs her insurance company and Seth is working remotely for an architectural company based in Cape Town. Whereas when Brian chose to be a meditation teacher he shut down his company completely.
20 04:47 Brian Wagner interview When the stage came I was fortunate enough to be in a position financially to be able to sustain myself. Nobody in Vipassana gets any form of income. Anything you do is in the form of Downer which is service. The decision for myself wouldn’t have been easy if I didn’t have financial means. In spirituality renunciation is always a big thing where you have to renunciation various things but in order to renunciate living in the world you have feed yourself.
21 05:25 Voice over Even though the Alfino have escaped the rate race the reality of packing everything you own in a camper van and living on the road isn’t always as Instagram perfect as you can imagine
22 05:35 Vlog Footage of Seth singing
23 05:42 Voice over Their picture perfect 1974 camper van broke down constantly
24 05:46 Seth and Cindy interview We were so naïve
Cindy: Yeah, we were so stupid
Seth: Like yeah it would probably break down
Cindy: Yeah, we will be fine and then it broke down and it wasn’t so easy. We got stuck in Pietritief for 2 solid weeks
25 06:01 Cindy vlogging to camera Cindy: and I really don’t have anything against Pietritief its just, I’ve just… I’m done with being here
26 06:08 Voice over Another challenge about living on the road was home schooling their 3 children
27 06:12 Seth and Cindy interview Seth: So yeah, I’m doing the home schooling. For me that was quite daunting because I wasn’t really involved in their home schooling
Cindy: Also, if we don’t do it well enough they would be set back a whole year and then what have we done to them instead of for them
28 06:27 Cindy in the forest We keep up with a journal so that they get the writing skills in and keep the memory alive so every day or every odd day they write just a page of what they have done and then draw a picture to like cement the memory you know
29 06:42 Seth and Cindy interview Seth: The kids have changed quite a bit
Cindy: And to say general knowledge they know things now. They have grown so much in their vocabulary and just their independence also
30 06:53 Voice over While the Alfino’s chose this alternative path to focus on bring their family together; brains life as a meditation teacher means he hardly spends any time at his Johannesburg home with his partner Kerry and their son
31 07:07 Voice over In 2018 Brian only spent 42 days at home so no choice is ever easy, everything takes sacrifice
32 07:16 Brian interview Its very difficult but Oliver his whole life that’s all he had you know, daddy come and daddy goes and he’s not there very long and he speaks to daddy on the phone on a regular basis and you can do a face to face call but the older Oliver gets the harder it is to leave him because now he’s become this real little character
33 07:43 Face video call with Brian, Kerry and Oliver Brian: Hello how are you guys? Did you do any inventions today?
Oliver: uhm nah
Brian: Nothing?
Oliver: I did do another invention
Brian: What did you invent?
Oliver: A bird’s trap
Brian: what are you going to do once you catch all of them?
Oliver: hm... make them my pets
Brian: oh, I see, that’s cool hey
Kerry: Remember if you catch it and make it your pets it’s not really your pet it’s your prisoner
34 08:13 Brian At home, there is a place where I mediate and often Kerry will find him sitting on the cushion, sitting with a shawl around him and she would say “ what are you doing?” and he would say “no I’m talking to dad” and I’m going to cry, I miss him a lot but then it’s my choice. You know there is nothing that is stopping me from saying I’m going to spend more time at home. My choice is to always go and conduct a course somewhere so it is my choice as a teacher you have to have a lot of unconditional love that you give to the student which you are teaching knowing that it’s just giving. So, you give something out without expecting anything back and for me that’s been a great great gift in my relationships and in my understanding with people because to be quite honest when I was in the business world I would do something and I would want something back from you.
35 09:10 Voice over Through their journey of finding true happiness both Brian and the Alfinos have radically change the perspective of what success means to them
36 09:20 Brian Success comes from within yourself and within your own being and how you feel about yourself
37 09:27 Cindy We are on the road again and it’s all good
38 09:31 Cindy and Seth Seth: Success now whereas before it was you know getting to that high position in the company and earning a lot of money
Cindy: and having a house that looks a certain way – Pinterest and throwing Pinterest parties you know none of that is important
Seth: it’s about family and enjoying each other
Cindy: relationships
Seth: and being a successful dad and husband
Cindy and you are doing a good job.

In spirituality renunciation is always a big thing where you have to renunciation various things but in order to renunciate living in the world you have feed yourself. 21 05:25 Voice over Even though the Alfino have escaped the rate race the reality of packing everything you own in a camper van and living on the road isn’t always as Instagram perfect as you can imagine 22 05:35 Vlog Footage of Seth singing 23 05:42 Voice over Their picture perfect 1974 camper van broke down constantly 24 05:46 Seth and Cindy interview We were so naïve Cindy: Yeah, we were so stupid Seth: Like yeah it would probably break down Cindy: Yeah, we will be fine and then it broke down and it wasn’t so easy. We got stuck in Pietritief for 2 solid weeks 25 06:01 Cindy vlogging to camera Cindy: and I really don’t have anything against Pietritief its just, I’ve just… I’m done with being here 26 06:08 Voice over Another challenge about living on the road was home schooling their 3 children 27 06:12 Seth and Cindy interview Seth: So yeah, I’m doing the home schooling. For me that was quite daunting because I wasn’t really involved in their home schooling Cindy: Also, if we don’t do it well enough they would be set back a whole year and then what have we done to them instead of for them 28 06:27 Cindy in the forest We keep up with a journal so that they get the writing skills in and keep the memory alive so every day or every odd day they write just a page of what they have done and then draw a picture to like cement the memory you know 29 06:42 Seth and Cindy interview Seth: The kids have changed quite a bit Cindy: And to say general knowledge they know things now. They have grown so much in their vocabulary and just their independence also 30 06:53 Voice over While the Alfino’s chose this alternative path to focus on bring their family together; brains life as a meditation teacher means he hardly spends any time at his Johannesburg home with his partner Kerry and their son 31 07:07 Voice over In 2018 Brian only spent 42 days at home so no choice is ever easy, everything takes sacrifice 32 07:16 Brian interview Its very difficult but Oliver his whole life that’s all he had you know, daddy come and daddy goes and he’s not there very long and he speaks to daddy on the phone on a regular basis and you can do a face to face call but the older Oliver gets the harder it is to leave him because now he’s become this real little character 33 07:43 Face video call with Brian, Kerry and Oliver Brian: Hello how are you guys? Did you do any inventions today? Oliver: uhm nah Brian: Nothing? Oliver: I did do another invention Brian: What did you invent? Oliver: A bird’s trap Brian: what are you going to do once you catch all of them? Oliver: hm... make them my pets Brian: oh, I see, that’s cool hey Kerry: Remember if you catch it and make it your pets it’s not really your pet it’s your prisoner 34 08:13 Brian At home, there is a place where I mediate and often Kerry will find him sitting on the cushion, sitting with a shawl around him and she would say “ what are you doing?” and he would say “no I’m talking to dad” and I’m going to cry, I miss him a lot but then it’s my choice. You know there is nothing that is stopping me from saying I’m going to spend more time at home. My choice is to always go and conduct a course somewhere so it is my choice as a teacher you have to have a lot of unconditional love that you give to the student which you are teaching knowing that it’s just giving. So, you give something out without expecting anything back and for me that’s been a great great gift in my relationships and in my understanding with people because to be quite honest when I was in the business world I would do something and I would want something back from you. 35 09:10 Voice over Through their journey of finding true happiness both Brian and the Alfinos have radically change the perspective of what success means to them 36 09:20 Brian Success comes from within yourself and within your own being and how you feel about yourself 37 09:27 Cindy We are on the road again and it’s all good 38 09:31 Cindy and Seth Seth: Success now whereas before it was you know getting to that high position in the company and earning a lot of money Cindy: and having a house that looks a certain way – Pinterest and throwing Pinterest parties you know none of that is important Seth: it’s about family and enjoying each other Cindy: relationships Seth: and being a successful dad and husband Cindy and you are doing a good job.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Life beyond the walls of societies norms and expectation, three people choose a path that works for them and the people they love
metadata.Summary: This story is a little Wild Wild country and a little eat pray love. Three people leave everything they have to to choose a new way of living; they reject all societies norms and expectations and create their own path. Forgoing their capital existence's to follow an alternative lifestyle, one that is centred around personal happiness for them and the people they love.
metadata.Further information: Character 1 Mary used to be an ER doctor, she was married to big time doctor and had the ‘perfect’ life, but she got divorced, her life fell apart and she needed a change. She started by doing a 10 day Vipassana silent retreat at the Vipassana Centre near Cape Town. All their courses are completely free. Everything at the center is based on donations from “old students” people that have done multiple courses and have a regular practice. Mary eventually landed up being invited to live permanently at the center. Vipassana is a non religious mindfulness way of living, it is the oldest form of Indian meditation. Modern day Vipassana practices are guided by one teacher MR Goenka: "Rather than converting people from one organised religion to another organised religion," said Mr. Goenka, "we should try to convert people from misery to happiness, from bondage to liberation and from cruelty to compassion." The centre is in the middle of nowhere. As a permanent resident Mary takes care of the kitchen. A daily routine starts with a video talk from the guru and a meditation in the morning then there are three group meals a day, all vegan. During the course no one can talk to each other and no-one is allowed digital devices and the dress code is respectful by covering body parts. During the course and in general followers of Vipasssana practice, no violence, no illicit substance, not thinking or speaking ill of anyone and no sex. Mary’s children are grown up and come visit her at the center. She has never been happier, she is glowing from the inside Character 2 Boggon has ten children and him and his wife have been married for 38 years, the whole family lives and work on the Rose family estate. It started with food, a mission to create food that provides energy. Boggon spent years researching how the foods people eat today are infact robbing us of energy instead of giving us energy. It then became a way of life, a family business and a spiritual quest. Boggons theories on food and the food they produce are based on biblical studies, he has looked at what god and his closest ate and gone back in time and studies early man in order to farm and create foods that sustain life, instead of deplete it. Spiritually Boggons believes that all you have to do is be kind and believe in god and the rest will happen. If you do badly to others it will come back ten fold. He has some crazy theories about how humans are being brain washed by Low-level frequencies being sent from an mine. Our water is poisoned as part of this brainwashing too. And that there are evil forces operating on very high frequencies keeping the world in chaos. The rose family have created a heaven for themselves in world that no longer made sense to them. They are now getting to the point where they want to share their way of life with a broader community and create a village This is what grandpa Rose, Boggons, says about their way of life: In a world full of toxins, chemicals, poisonous foods, opposition and plenty of negativity! Our purpose is to provide all the knowledge we have accumulated, so that you too, can be FREE!!! Nobody in our family goes to doctors, are on any prescriptions or suffer from any sort of illnesses and we want you to experience that!!! Food is medicine! Character 3 A family that quit everything and are living on the road with their children. Home schooling them and seeing the world, while working remotely.
